styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow, red, vertical signboard with a rounded cap and a white 'guk-bap' text panel. It has 9 visible tones per full tile, which is above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark red-brown rather than black. That matches the references. Shading is limited: the body shows roughly 3-4 red steps (a highlight edge, mid, dark, and a deep edge), while the references show about 5. The body is a fairly smooth fill with little grain, and the cap and text band give the only extra detail. It is a clean, acceptable prop, but thinner and simpler than kiosk-a and vending-a, which are the closest comparisons. Since the piece is a thin standing sign, sparseness alone is not grounds to fail. However, the shallow ramp on the large red body and the plain surface make it read slightly flatter than the references. In doubt, fail.
